**Seven stops, in the order you meet them.** The last column is there to be ticked: printed, or in
the Word copy, this table is the checklist for one commission.

| Where you are | Where to read it | What you do there | What you leave behind | Done |
|----------------|-------------------|-------------------------------------|-----------------------|-----|
| You need analysis to make a decision | [Phase 1. Engagement and scoping](/guidance/01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd) | State the decision, the deadline, and how certain the answer needs to be. Identify the key stakeholders. Expect the analyst to challenge a request that arrives already framed as an output | The decision, the question and the deadline, written down where the analyst can work from them | ☐ |
| How much assurance does this need? | [Deciding your assurance level](/guidance/07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) | Score it with the analyst. The score is about what an error would do, not about how hard the work is, and it is agreed at scoping rather than described afterwards | The completed assurance level decision sheet, and the Business Critical answer recorded either way | ☐ |
| Is there time for the assurance this needs? | [Three things only you can do](/guidance/06-roles/commissioner.qmd#three-things-only-you-can-do) | Making sure there is enough time and resource for the assurance the level requires is your responsibility. Where time and resource constrain the approach, you need to understand the risks that follow | A schedule with the assurance in it, including the reviewer's own time | ☐ |
| Is the design right before the work starts? | [Phase 2. Design](/guidance/02-design/index.qmd) | Approve the design before work proceeds. The critical friend confirms the approach answers the question and that the assurance planned is at the right level; you confirm it meets your need | The approved design and plan, and your approval recorded against it | ☐ |
| The analysis is running | [Phase 3. Analysis](/guidance/03-analysis/index.qmd) | Stay available for clarification and review any change of design or method the analyst raises. Resist changing the question late. Deadline pressure is resolved by narrowing the question, not by lowering the level | A decision log entry for anything you changed, and the reason for it | ☐ |
| Can I use this? | [Phase 4. Delivery and sign-off](/guidance/04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd) | Confirm the analysis is likely to meet your need, understand and apply its limitations, and use it as specified. You approve the results for release and are accountable for their use and dissemination | Your approval, and the quality assurance statement attached to the output | ☐ |
| Did it do any good? | [Phase 5. Review](/guidance/05-review/index.qmd) | Above Level 1 the review is yours to own, with the analyst. At Levels 3 and 4 BCA the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer joins you.<br><br>Did it inform the decision, is it still used, and should it be decommissioned? | The review record, kept with the project record | ☐ |

**One branch, after the assurance level stop.** Deciding whether the analysis is Business Critical is
yours. Any one impact dimension at 4 makes it so. If you and the analyst cannot agree, it goes to the
Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead.
